chapter: Family, education and the gap years
title: Playing with Herbert Leary and at the Dew Drop while raising a family
summary: In the gap years she played about five years with Herbert Leary's orchestra, then solo and in a small group at the Dew Drop, staying with stationary bands.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: During that time, did you, I know you wouldn't have given up music, but did you play out in the public at all with any bands or by yourself or… Do you mean before I came to… No, in that period between 1935 when you were raising your family. Oh, yes.

Yes. I just wondered… I was with another band a while and then I played… Which band was if you don't mind? I was with Herbert Leary's orchestra for about five years during that time. And then I played solo at a nightclub, a colored nightclub. Where was that? Which? The Dew Drop.
Oh, yes, right over… I played over there.

And then I played, well we had a group too. We had a little group over there about six pieces. I played there about two years. So I was still in music, but I couldn't travel at that time. Therefore, I only played with bands who were stationary. Did you do much teaching?
